rationale:
Rendering and palette pass, not a redraw. The silhouette, pose, masses and front-facing cue are byte-identical to v1 - every transparent pixel is still transparent and every opaque pixel is still opaque; only the colour under each pixel changed. Colour count goes 24 -> 50.

The palette is organised as ten material ramps rather than a flat swatch list, and each ramp shifts hue as it descends instead of only losing value: warmer and yellower toward the upper-left key, cooler and plum-ward into shadow. That is where most of the new colours went.

- Coat and helmet shell, 7 steps, #8b9b93 -> #1f292d: lit green-grey canvas turning blue-grey in shadow.
- Rust livery, 7 steps, #f0b184 -> #48212a: peach light that falls to a cold plum rather than to brown.
- Skin, 7 steps, #f4c9a2 -> #341b26, with the v1 plum #573240 kept as the turn on the shadow side of the head.
- Metal, 5 steps: warm steel specular #b8b1a8 down to cold #24232c.
- Leather, 4 steps: warm worn edge #5c4c45 down to #171217.
- Trousers, 4 steps pulled toward violet (#565060) so the legs read as a different cloth from the coat instead of merging with it.
- Goggle glass and bone, 5 steps ending in #46605f; teal emission, 5 steps with a hot #74e8d4 core.
- Three inks. #120b10 remains the deepest anchor and still owns every contact edge and underside. #241a28 is a lifted ink used only on upper-left-facing contour, so hard corners - helmet crown, shoulder caps, cuffs, cannon spine, boot tops - carry a rim without weakening the outline. #2b1f2c is a soft plum seam ink for interior material transitions such as the under-brim band and the goggle bridge.
- Three grime values (#8b7b71 / #6a5a52 / #3a3230) chosen to sit within a few points of the luminance of the surfaces they land on, so dirt reads as a hue shift rather than punching a hole.

Forms turn now. The helmet dome bands diagonally across five steps from a lit crown to a shadowed lower-right, with a two-pixel dent (light lip over dark shadow) and a warm dirt smudge in the light band. Each goggle lens carries four steps plus a single specular pixel and still holds the brightest values in the sprite, which is what the front-facing cue depends on. The coat gains a light top plane across the shoulders, a diagonal cloth fold running down-right off the collar, a deliberately broken rim-light column on its left edge so it does not read as a painted stripe, and a hem in three shadow steps with dust ground into it. The chest cross is shaded across three pale steps so it reads as a thick painted mark with thickness rather than a decal.

Wear is placed, not sprinkled: a chipped-paint pixel on each rust sleeve, a hard notch bitten out of the brim, a scuffed knuckle on each glove, a polished buckle, mud on both boots and a smear on one thigh. Seams are real material transitions rather than colour changes - the rust sleeve ends in a darkened seam row before the metal cuff, the cuff's darkest step meets the glove's lit top edge, the belt's dark rust band meets leather, and the trousers drop a full value into the boot.

Identity budget is unchanged: roughly 70% grey-teal coat, 25% rust livery, 5% teal emission, anchored on #120b10. No magenta, no chartreuse. What it still sacrifices is unchanged too - the figure is planted and ready rather than mid-action, and the torso still spends less silhouette than the head and the weapon.
frontFacingCue:
Unchanged in structure, sharpened in colour. A value stack down the head that the back of a skull cannot produce, reading top to bottom: a shell dome that bands from a lit crown (#5b6a63) to a shadowed lower-right (#1f292d); a rust brim that juts two pixels wider than the crown on both sides and runs its own light-to-dark ramp (#f0b184 at the lit tip through #48212a at the shadow end); a hard dark band under the brim which is now graded, soft plum #2b1f2c on the lit side to #120b10 on the shadow side; then the brightest band in the entire sprite - twin goggle lenses, each carrying a #fbf7ee specular in its upper-left corner, then #ece0cf, then #bccbc7, then #718c8b, then #46605f in the lower-right, with a dark bridge between them; then a lit skin face plane with a #f4c9a2 brow highlight on the upper-left and a #6d3b31 nose shadow running down the centre; then the mouthpiece, a dark bar with a single lit pixel on its left end so it reads as moulded rather than as a slot; then a jaw that tapers over three rows to a chin; then plum under-chin shadow; then a 6px skin neck, darker than the face because the head casts onto it, flanked by transparency.

Two things still enforce separation from the shoulders. The neck is a real 2-row, 6px column that is 14px narrower than the head above it and 24px narrower than the shoulders below, with transparent pixels on both sides. And nothing rises above the shoulder line at all - no pack, no hood, no collar peak. The single teal pixel pair at the collar centre is now a two-value emitter (#74e8d4 core beside #31b3a4) sitting over a dark #17464b / #1e7a78 housing on the row beneath, so it reads unambiguously as a front-mounted status light.
smallCheck:
Yes, and it survives better than v1 did. I box-downscaled to 21x28 with alpha-weighted averaging and inspected at 8x, and also checked 3x.

What holds at 28px: the head silhouette with its wide brim; the goggle band as a bright horizontal slash, still the first thing the eye lands on; the pale face beneath it; the rust shoulder caps as two distinct orange blocks; the chest cross as a light mark on rust; the injector-cannon as a dark diagonal with a legible teal glint at lower-left; and - new in this pass - the legs, which now separate from the coat hem because the trousers were pulled toward violet while the coat stayed green-grey. In v1 the lower half collapsed into one dark mass; the hue split does most of the work that value alone could not.

What is lost, as expected: the placed wear - chips, buckle, mud, the helmet dent - all averages away, and the boots merge into the leg mass below the ankle. The right glove still merges into the torso silhouette. The extra interior ramp steps mostly survive as smoother gradients rather than as distinguishable bands, which is the correct failure mode - nothing turns to mush or reads as noise, because every added colour is a small step inside a material rather than a new hue competing for attention.

At the authored 48x64 and at any integer scale of it, none of this is a concern.
